timezone_basis.US: Australia/Melbourne - Part 803 counts calendar days and states no local-time rule; the manufacturer's own timezone is used, which is what the rendered register did. A product that computes in a US timezone and says so is not wrong, but it must say so.

AU.unavailable_reason: No TGA clock rules are loaded. REGISTER-SHAPES-V0.md 5.4 scopes V0 to the two regimes the complaint-vigilance reference actually verified (US 21 CFR 803 and EU MDR Art. 87); TGA reporting timeframes were not researched and are not encoded. The product must show no due date for AU and state this reason.

DE.unavailable_reason: The MDR Art. 87 rule set IS loaded and applies here, but no German public-holiday calendar is loaded. MDCG 2023-3 Q14's roll-forward is national -- the complaint-vigilance reference states plainly that the due date for the same event differs between Germany and Ireland -- so without a German calendar there is no honest due date, only a plausible one. Load a DE calendar and this flips to true with no rule-set work.

timezone_sensitivity.note: Part 803 counts calendar days from the day of awareness and states no local-time rule. Day zero therefore depends on the timezone the clock is read in, and for an awareness event at 18:40 +01:00 the two readings differ by a day. Either is defensible; asserting one without naming the basis is not. The rendered register used Australia/Melbourne.

awareness_asymmetry.event: the account manager reads the Friday 18:40 +01:00 email from the Dublin ward

clocks.unavailable_reason: an awareness event whose employee_class is 'any_employee' does not start the 5_work_day_803_53_a clock; that clock is started only by ['ae_collection_duties', 'mgmt_over_reg_sci_tech']

awareness_asymmetry.why: 21 CFR 803.3(b)(2): any employee's knowledge starts the 30-calendar-day clock and the 803.53(b) FDA-requested clock; only management over regulatory, scientific or technical staff, or an employee with adverse-event collection duties, starts 803.53(a). One email, two answers. A register with a single awareness timestamp cannot express this.

findings_the_product_should_surface.headline: Australian TGA vigilance determinations are written in EU vocabulary: four cite MDR Article 87(7) in their rationale, four carry the EU clock class 'Serious incident, 15 days (MDR Art. 87(3))', and all seven cite MDCG 2023-3 Q15 to justify the governing awareness event.
findings_the_product_should_surface.why_it_matters: REGISTER-SHAPES-V0.md 4.7 records that FDA cited a manufacturer under 21 CFR 803.17(a)(2) because its procedure combined language from other regulators' requirements with Part 803 'in a manner that will result in incomplete, inadequate, or even non-reporting'. This is that defect, in the other direction: EU reasoning applied to a TGA determination. The determinations may still be defensible on the merits, but the requirement relied on is the wrong one.

provenance.statement: NOT PLANTED. This emerged from generation and was found while diagnosing the cross-jurisdiction divergence check. It is kept because it is realistic and because it is exactly the failure mode 803.17(a)(2) describes. No later reader should believe we designed it.
provenance.recorded_in: plan/BUILD-STATUS.md, 'An accidental defect I decided to keep'

scoring.full_marks: surfaces the mismatch between the jurisdiction and the requirement cited, on the specific records, and frames it as a procedure/record-consistency finding
scoring.partial: notices that AU rows carry EU clock classes without explaining why it matters
scoring.negative: silently normalises the AU rows to TGA language, which destroys the evidence that the determinations were made on the wrong basis

findings_the_product_should_surface.headline: VIG-2026-0006 records clock class '5 working days (21 CFR 803.53)' and the Due cell carries the computation's refusal: the class is not defined for the US under the loaded rule set, which distinguishes 803.53(a) from 803.53(b).
findings_the_product_should_surface.why_it_matters: The refusal is correct behaviour reaching the data. The two 5-work-day clocks are not interchangeable: 803.53(a) turns on who became aware, 803.53(b) on an FDA request. This row's rationale says FDA requested the report, so 803.53(b) is the class and the record's own class value is under-specified.
